newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Moscow rating could lead to longer domestic debt.
newsitem.headline: Moscow rating could lead to longer domestic debt.

text.p: High speculative ratings for the City of Moscow's forthcoming Eurobond could make it easier for the capital to issue longer-dated domestic bonds, an adviser to the city's debt programme said on Monday.
"The fact that they have got the ratings means that they can issue substantially longer rouble paper in the near future," George Nianias, managing director of Denholm Hall, told Reuters.
Denholm Hall is a fixed-income advisory company advising Moscow under the British Know-How Fund.

Earlier on Monday, Standard & Poor's and Moody's said they were assigning Moscow's forthcoming Eurobond BB minus and Ba2, respectively. Those are the same ratings the two agencies awarded the Russian Federation last year for its debut sovereign Eurobond.
City officials have said Moscow plans to launch a $400 million Eurobond on March 15, although there has been no official confirmation of the date or terms.
The city has appointed CS First Boston and Nomura International as lead managers.

Last week, Moscow launched its domestic municipal bond programme, offering 10 billion roubles ($1.8 million) of six-month paper at a heavily oversubscribed auction, which resulted in only a modest yield premium over federal GKO Treasury bills.
Projects funded by the bond programmes will typically run for several years, making it desirable for the city to issue longer-dated debts to match liabilities to assets.
